page: Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-intel is a virtual server in the High Performance family, featuring 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance allocates a shared CPU configuration with a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB per core, and includes a local storage allocation of 180 GB NVMe SSD. No GPU hardware is bundled with this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average single-core capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1456.98 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1161.0. However, multi-core performance is weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 5760.92 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3726.0, which is a direct consequence of the shared CPU allocation. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 409.04 GB/sec, large-block uncached read bandwidth drops to a weak 36.98 GB/sec. Database operations and static web serving throughput also fall into the lower performance tiers.

This server provides a budget-friendly entry point for workloads requiring local NVMe storage and moderate single-threaded processing. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU model, which introduces resource contention risks and limits sustained multi-threaded performance. Consequently, this instance is best suited for lightweight web serving, development environments, basic Redis caching operations, and non-critical background tasks rather than intensive multi-threaded computing or large-scale database hosting.
